Thanks again for the call earlier — great alignment on the high-level flow. Short recap and concrete next steps so we all have the same checklist: 

Summary (one-liner)
- Finlytics will route user documents to a Redwood-managed embedder for semantic search, then use a reranker + structured-output model for claim extraction. Goal: production pilot in Q4.

Key technical items we agreed to validate
- SDK bootstrap & auth: Finlytics wants a short live demo of SDK auth flows (API key + optional OIDC).
- Routing & latency: target median 120ms for embedder ops from their EU region (they may start in US).
- Structured output: strict JSON schema for extracted claims; failure modes must be detectable and retried or fallback to human review.
- Embedding / reranker: evaluate cost vs. quality on a 50k doc sample.

Immediate asks (owners + deadlines)
- Marissa: share a first-pass JSON schema + validation approach by EOD 10/06. (I will attach the template.)
- Dev: provide SDK quickstart + suggested auth snippet and token rotation guidance by 10/07.
- Sergio: propose routing fallback policy and KV cache sizing notes by 10/08.
- Finlytics: send the 50k sample manifest and any PII redaction rules.

Attachments referenced: finlytics_structout_schema_v1.json (schema stub), redwood_sdk_auth_quickstart.md (auth snippet), routing_kvcache_diagram.png (rough diagram).

Next meeting: propose 30 minutes next week — suggest 10/11 or 10/12.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Quick post-call recap + next technical steps (schema + auth TL;DR)

Great — thanks for the clarifications. Attached are the three stubs we discussed. High-level notes inline below and an implementation example.

Attachment: finlytics_structout_schema_v1.json (schema thumbnail) — top-level shape:
{
  "id": "string",
  "document_id": "string",
  "claims": [
    {"type": "string", "confidence": "number", "start_offset": "integer", "end_offset": "integer", "metadata": {}}
  ]
}

Validation strategy (suggested)
- Pre-parse: strict JSON parse with a schema validator (we recommend Ajv in Node, jsonschema in Python).
- Constrained decoding: model should be prompted with deterministic decoding (top_p=0, temperature=0) for schema-conforming outputs. Use token-level stopping sequences to avoid trailing commentary.
- Post-validate: run schema validation; if failure -> attempt structured re-parse (single-shot retry with additional prompt: "Return only a JSON object that conforms to the schema.")
- Retry policy: 2 immediate re-tries with stricter prompt + then move to "review" queue. Add an idempotency key on the request for safe retries.

Auth & SDK bootstrap (brief)
- Quickstart attached (redwood_sdk_auth_quickstart.md) shows:
  - how to exchange OIDC token for a short-lived inference credential,
  - example header: Authorization: Bearer <redwood_api_key-or-token>,
  - guidance for token rotation and recommended TTL (15m for short-lived, 60m max for session-bound).

Snippet (Node)
- const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, region: 'us-east-1' })
- await client.embed({ model: 'redwood-embedder-v2', input: docs })

Routing & fallback (TL;DR)
- Route by priority: (1) dedicated pool (SLA) if org has committed capacity, (2) hosted low-latency variant, (3) quantized cheaper model for low-priority async jobs.
- KV cache sizing: start with a 100k entry cache for common prefixes; we can model hit-rate from your 50k sample.

Next steps (concrete items)
- Marissa: finalize schema + push to Drive (I did, link below).
- Dev: see TODOs in-line for SDK examples; please add an example for idempotent retry headers.
- Sergio: draft fallback routing policy and a short SLO doc for 95th percentile.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/finlytics-integration-spec (schema + diagrams)
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/FIN-4219

Thanks — I propose a short tech sync (30m) on 10/07 for SDK/auth + routing. If that works, Dev & Sergio can lead.

—Marissa

Subject: Re: Quick post-call recap + next technical steps (implementation notes)

Thanks — adding concrete implementation notes from the SDK/runtime side (keeping for the sync and for Finlytics to review):

1) Constrained decoding patterns
- For strict JSON outputs we recommend: temperature=0, top_p=1 (or top_p=0.0 in runtimes that accept it for deterministic output), max_new_tokens tuned to expected schema length + small buffer. Use explicit stop sequences like "\n}END" and instruct the model to close the JSON object.
- If your dataset contains long claims that exceed token limits, return a reference skeleton with offsets and call a detail endpoint to expand.

2) Validation + retry flow (implementation)
- Step A: call -> model -> parse as JSON -> validate via schema validator.
- Step B: on failure, immediately make a second call with the same idempotency key and an augmented system instruction: "You returned invalid JSON. Return only the JSON object matching this schema: <schema>. No additional text."
- Step C: if second attempt fails, run a lightweight heuristic fixer (trim trailing commas, remove commentary tokens) and attempt a local parse. If still failing, tag as "needs_triage" and forward to manual queue.
- Backoff policy: immediate retry (0s), second retry after 500ms, then escalate.

3) Observability hooks
- Emit a validation.status metric (success|fixed|failed), validation.attempts count, and validation.latency. Add the raw model token outputs as compressed logs only for triage.

4) Idempotency & dedup
- Use a request_id computed from (document_id + schema_hash + attempt_count). Supply as header X-Redwood-Request-Id. This keeps retries safe across retries and avoids duplicate charges.

I'll prepare a short sample PR for the SDK examples and drop in the Drive folder by tomorrow morning.

—Dev

Redwood Inference

Morning — pairing on delivery timeline and fallback policy. Short plan below: 

Pilot rollout (2 weeks) - Week 1: sandbox run with 10k docs (validate schema failures, collect 95p latency).
- Week 2: expanded run with 50k sample and reranker A/B (control: existing ranker; variant: redwood-reranker-v1).

Fallback policy (implementation detail)
- If embedder latency > 500ms OR 95p > 800ms -> route to async backfill path and mark the session as degraded.
- For schema validation: after 2 failed attempts mark as "review" and surface to a small human-review queue with the original text & model outputs.

SLOs & metrics we will populate for the SOW
- Embedder: median latency target 120ms (goal), 95th < 800ms (SLA requirement).
- Structured-output: validation.success_rate >= 98% for production traffic; during pilot we accept down to 95% as we iterate on prompts.

I'll draft the brief SOW language for procurement and share by EOD 10/07 so procurement@finlytics.com has something to review.

—Sergio
Director, Platform Engineering
